Tyler-like map tiles, Makie compiled to WebAssembly

Drag to pan, and fling to keep it moving. Zoom with the wheel, a trackpad pinch, a two-finger pinch, a double click or tap (Shift+double click zooms out), or the ± buttons. Zoom levels snap to whole numbers when a gesture ends. The view is owned by a small map camera written in Julia and compiled with WasmCodegen.jl under verify=:error. That camera handles drag, inertia, pinch, wheel, double tap and snapping. On each change it picks the visible tiles, downloads the missing ones with Downloads.request, decodes the PNGs in pure Julia, and updates Makie image! plots. WGLMakie's own three.js client draws the result. The page's JavaScript only forwards raw pointer and wheel events and runs the animation frames.

Tiles are downloaded live from tile.openstreetmap.org by the wasm module (plain Downloads.request, run by the browser's fetch). Only the visible tiles (at most 14) and eight lower-zoom background tiles are requested, after a gesture ends (never during one, and nothing is prefetched); a tile that fails is not retried, and tiles seen again come from the browser's HTTP cache.

Requirements: WebAssembly GC, exception handling, and JS Promise Integration (WebAssembly.Suspending), which lets the module wait for a download. Chrome 137 or later has all three. Without JSPI, or if the page's CSP lacks 'wasm-unsafe-eval', the status line above shows the error.
